methodology.environment: Fresh cp312 venv with system-site-packages; python -S and explicit venv-site, hrl-site, scripts path order prevented editable/source leakage. A venv-local pymimir symlink preserved the native wheel dylib rpath.
methodology.path_order: Forward in rounds 1 and 3; reverse in round 2. Current same-process backend order was Pymimir/PyTyr, PyTyr/Pymimir, Pymimir/PyTyr.
methodology.transition_alignment: Each backend BFS-collected real (current, successor) pairs from the same Blocks/smedium scenario, then cycled the backend-local pool to exactly 32 transitions. Fixture setup and encoder construction were outside timed sections.
methodology.aggregate: Median of the three per-round medians; current/original ratio and percent change use those aggregates.
methodology.acceptance: At most 5% current Pymimir regression for batch paths; at most 10% for single-loop and stream end-to-end paths.

packaging_validation.pytyr_build_command: MIFROST_BUILD_BACKENDS=pytyr MIFROST_WHEEL_GENERATE_STUBS=1 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=2 conda run --no-capture-output -n hrl python -m pip wheel . --no-deps --wheel-dir /private/tmp/bifrost-transition-pytyr-wheel

optimization.reason: Every current Pymimir path passed its acceptance gate; no transition fast path was introduced.

process_memory.metric: resource.ru_maxrss bytes on macOS; external /usr/bin/time -l maximum resident set size bytes retained independently
process_memory.interpretation: Peak footprint and maximum RSS are process-level context for the benchmark runs, not per-encoder allocation measurements; no acceptance threshold is applied to them.
